title: Tenant-aware embedding dark-launch, versioning, and deprecation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Create a reproducible, tenant-aware playbook for onboarding new embedding model variants, running dark-launch / shadow traffic experiments, versioning contracts, and executing safe deprecations. The playbook must balance semantic quality, tail latency, and cluster economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Scope covers model aliasing, per-tenant traffic shaping, automated rollback thresholds, KV-cache compatibility, embedding dimensionality projection, and deprecation embargo timelines.
background: We frequently onboard new embedding models for quality/efficiency improvements. Past incidents (high p95 latency during large-tenant swap, silent semantic regressions on long-tail tenants) showed we need finer-grained controls and deterministic rollback rules. This ticket consolidates learnings into an automated, tenant-aware dark-launch and versioning flow that integrates with Console metrics and Optimize recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: A documented dark-launch sequence that supports per-tenant shadowing and configurable sampling (0.1% -> 100%),
Automated SLI checks: semantic-delta and latency-delta gates evaluated per-tenant and aggregated, with configurable thresholds and automatic rollback action when breached,
A version aliasing contract that guarantees stable input/output dimensionality or provides projection shim with bounded cosine drift,
Telemetry dashboards and alerting: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, semantic-similarity histograms, quality regression counts, and cost delta,
Compatibility fallbacks: automatic routing to quantized/legacy variant if memory or tail-latency thresholds are exceeded,
A deprecation runway process including embargo windows, notice generation to customer console, and automatic sticky routing for pinned tenants.
tasks: Design telemetry schema for per-tenant semantic similarity probes and latency buckets
Implement shadow router changes: per-tenant sampling rate and adaptive ramp
Add projection shim for embedding dimensionality differences and record projection error metric
Create automated gating engine: evaluates semantic and latency SLIs and triggers rollback/runforward according to policy
Integrate with Console: per-tenant rollout UI, manual override, and deprecation notices
End-to-end smoke tests and chaos tests with large-tenant replicas to verify tail behavior
Write runbook for oncall: escalation path, rollback command examples, and customer communication templates
decisions: Use cosine similarity + KL on normalized score distributions as the primary semantic delta metric (decision made 2026-02-05).
Per-tenant p95 delta threshold = 20ms for Hosted tiers, 10ms for Dedicated SLA tenants; breach counts over a 30m window will trigger automated mitigation (decision 2026-02-18).
Support projection shim when dimensionality differs by at most 128 dims; larger differences require model aliasing and explicit migration plan (decision 2026-02-25).
Fallback order: pinned_model -> quantized_4bit_variant -> legacy_variant. Fallbacks are recorded and surfaced in Console.
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Ticket opened. Kickoff with ML Infra, Runtime, and Console stakeholders. Agreed on per-tenant approach.

2026-02-18: Gating engine PoC completed; initial test shows correct rollback on synthetically injected latency spike. Observability panel prototype ready (console.redwood/internal/dash/emb-onboard-642318).

2026-02-28: Projection shim implemented in serving runtime (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/1897). Unit tests + projection error metric added. Discovered 0.03 average projection cosine drift for 64->512 dims in bench dataset.

2026-03-05: Large-tenant chaos run performed with a 10x request burst; quantized fallback prevented p99 spikes but increased semantic-delta slightly for 2 tenants. Collected feedback and adjusted thresholds.

notes: Risk: Projection shim can mask semantic regressions. Mitigation: require shadow evaluations and minimum cosine similarity lower bound before allowing traffic ramp.
Risk: Dedicated tenants expect tighter latency; will mark tenants with SLA tag to enforce stricter thresholds.
Operational: Add a Console action to immediately pin a tenant to a specific model alias for 7-day sticky routing.
Follow-up: Create a small eval harness for long-tail languages and domain-specific corpora to catch niche regressions early.
